scope.flow: HypoVault share accounting: constructor sets totalSupply to 1,000,000 without minting balances, then deposit and withdrawal formulas scale by totalSupply

statements.text: HypoVault's constructor sets totalSupply to 1,000,000 shares.
The 1,000,000 shares set in the constructor are never minted to any account, so they have zero corresponding balances.
Both the share-minting and redemption formulas use totalSupply as a scaling factor.
Deposits over-mint: new entrants receive more shares than their fair pro-rata allocation, diluting incumbents.
Withdrawals under-pay: redemptions release fewer assets per share because the denominator is artificially inflated.
Value is stealthily skimmed into the void over time, permanently disadvantaging honest users.
The ERC-20 invariant totalSupply == sum(balanceOf[]) must hold so that share-minting and redemption formulas fairly prorate deposits, withdrawals, and profits.

ambiguities: No concrete deposit or withdrawal transaction is described; the over-mint and under-pay effects are stated as consequences of the constructor state rather than observed executions.
The report does not state who triggers the dilution or whether any actor must hold a prior balance, so no attacker action is supported.
The exact deposit and redemption formulas and their operands are not given, so the quantitative over-mint/under-pay relation cannot be expressed numerically.
The 'permanently disadvantaging' and 'skims value into the void' claims are not quantified and are treated as potential downstream effects.
